Recognizing akathisia

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Soon after starting metoclopramide, a patient feels unable to sit still, repeatedly paces and describes distressing inner restlessness. There is no elevated mood, grandiosity or sustained muscle spasm. Which adverse effect best matches this presentation?

  1. Oculogyric crisis
  2. Peripheral neuropathy
  3. Akathisia
  4. Acute mania
  5. Tardive orofacial dyskinesia
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Akathisia

Akathisia is motor restlessness with subjective inner distress and can follow dopamine receptor blockade.

Understanding the options

Akathisia
Akathisia is motor restlessness with subjective inner distress and can follow dopamine receptor blockade.
Acute mania
The absence of mood and behavioral features argues against mania.
Tardive orofacial dyskinesia
Tardive dyskinesia produces involuntary movements rather than primarily inner restlessness.
Oculogyric crisis
An oculogyric crisis is sustained eye deviation.
Peripheral neuropathy
Neuropathy causes sensory symptoms or weakness, not this urge to move.
